newsitem.title: USA: U.S. bank derivatives revenues fall 11 pct in Q3.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bank derivatives revenues fall 11 pct in Q3.

text.p: U.S. banks garnered $1.7 billion in revenue from derivatives trading activities in the third quarter, an 11 percent drop from the same period last year, Office of the Comptroller of the Currency said Monday.

The decline was most dramatic on foreign exchange contract trading, where revenue fell to $514 million from $761 million last year, OCC said. Interest rate contract trading revenues rose modestly to $990 million from $964 million.
Equity derivatives trading revenues dropped substantially to $93 million from $211 million. Revenues from commodity contracts rose twenty-fold to $137 million from $7 million.

The data was drawn from call reports filed with regulators by commercial banks, OCC said. Trading revenues included cash and off-balance sheet derivatives activities but not on-balance sheet activities, OCC said.

Notional amounts of derivatives held by banks continued to grow in the third quarter, OCC said. Notional amounts indicate the level of derivatives activity but do not necessarily reveal the amount banks have at risk, OCC said.
Banks notional value of interest rate contracts rose to $8.7 trillion from $8 trillion in the same quarter last year. Forex notional value rose to $5.4 trillion from $5.2 trillion.
Among smaller niches, notional value of gold contracts rose to $64.1 billion from $40.3 billion and notional value of other precious metals fell to $4.9 billion from $5 billion.
Notional value of other commodity contracts rose to $50.1 billion from $45.8 billion, OCC said.
Notional value of equity contracts fell to $80.7 billion $87.2 billion.

Non-performing derivatives contracts remained at nominal levels, OCC said. For all banks, the book value of contracts due 30 days or more aggregated to $21 million, or 0.009 percent of total derivatives credit exposures.
During the third quarter, banks with derivatives contracts reported year-to-date charge-offs of $37 million from credit losses, OCC said.

Banks continue to reduce credit exposure on derivatives by using netting agreements, OCC said. In the third quarter, netting gave banks a 46.6 percent reduction in credit exposure, compared to 43.4 percent in the same period last year.
